caption: A dropper elevator: the hopper under the input chest feeds the bottom of a column of six droppers facing up; the top one pushes into the output chest five blocks above the input chest. One observer clock fires the whole column: the observer whose back touches the second dropper pulses every 6 gt with its partner (placed last: a player starts the clock by placing it), and a chain of four observers carries each pulse up to the observer powering the fifth dropper, 4 gt later in the period. A powered dropper powers the droppers above and below it, so each powered dropper fires three. The 4 gt keep the upper group off whenever the lower group's top dropper is updated: that dropper also reads the upper group's power (quasi-connectivity: a dropper is powered when the block above it would be) and would otherwise stay triggered and never fire again.

A dropper elevator 4 blocks up (11 blocks): the hopper under the input chest feeds a column of droppers facing up, the top one pushing into the output chest. One observer clock (6 gt) fires the column: its observer at the second dropper is placed last (a player starts the clock by placing it), so its partner leads by 2 gt; a chain of observers facing down climbs from the partner a block every 2 gt, and an observer every two blocks fires the next three droppers 4 gt after the ones below (a hard-powered dropper powers the ones above and below it). A dropper also reads the power of the dropper two above (quasi-connectivity), so each group must be off whenever the group below turns off.
